content: A single dose of tadalafil should not exceed 10 mg within a 72-hour period. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of talazoparib by mechanisms involving other pathways (refer to specific comments). If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for potential adverse reactions. Atazanavir and tamoxifen interact by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat reduces the effects of tamoxifen by altering its metabolism through CYP3A4. Avoid or use alternative drugs. CYP3A4 inhibition decreases the conversion of tamoxifen to its active metabolite, N-desmethyl tamoxifen, which has similar biological activity. Atazanavir increases tamsulosin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat elevates tamsulosin levels through the same mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Atazanavir increases tasimelteon levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Tazemetostat decreases atazanavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. It also reduces cobicistat levels through the same mechanism. Conversely, cobicistat increases tazemetostat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Atazanavir also increases tazemetostat levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration of tazemetostat with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Tecovirimat decreases atazanavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer and may reduce cobicistat levels. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if coadministered. Atazanavir increases temsirolimus levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also elevates temsirolimus levels through the same mechanism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. After discontinuing cobicistat, allow a one-week washout period before increasing the cobicistat dose to its original level. Atazanavir increases teniposide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Cobicistat also increases teniposide levels through the same mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Tenofovir DF decreases atazanavir levels through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Both atazanavir and tenofovir DF increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Tepotinib increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If concomitant use is unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended in its approved product labeling. Cobicistat increases terbinafine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also elevates terbinafine levels through the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Cobicistat increases tezacaftor levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also elevates tezacaftor levels through the same mechanism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen if coadministered with a strong CYP3A inhibitor. Cobicistat increases theophylline levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also elevates theophylline levels through the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Cobicistat increases thioridazine levels through other mechanisms (refer to specific comments). Modify therapy and monitor closely. A dose reduction of antipsychotics metabolized by CYP3A or CYP2D6 may be needed upon coadministration. Atazanavir increases ticagrelor levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ticagrelor is metabolized by CYP3A4/5. Cobicistat also increases ticagrelor levels through the same mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Atazanavir enhances the effects of timolol through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Cobicistat also increases timolol levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Atazanavir increases tinidazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also elevates tinidazole levels through the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Cobicistat increases tipranavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir and tipranavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Atazanavir also elevates tipranavir levels through the same mechanism. Tipranavir increases atazanavir and cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Cobicistat increases tisotumab vedotin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also elevates tisotumab vedotin levels through the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Cobicistat increases tofacitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also elevates tofacitinib levels through the same mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg once daily when coadministered with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. Atazanavir increases tolterodine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also elevates tolterodine levels through the same mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases tolvatptan levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also elevates tolvatptan levels through the same mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. Atazanavir increases tramadol levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also elevates tramadol levels through the same mechanism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. A reduced tramadol dose may be required. Atazanavir increases trazodone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also elevates trazodone levels through other mechanisms (refer to specific comments). Use caution and monitor closely. Cobicistat increases triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also elevates triamcinolone levels through the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Cobicistat increases triazolam levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also elevates triazolam levels by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Cobicistat increases trimipramine levels by affecting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also elevates trimipramine levels through the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to achieve the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor its response during coadministration. Tucatinib increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Cobicistat increases zanubrutinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also elevates zanubrutinib levels through the same mechanism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce zanubrutinib to 80 mg once daily if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Atazanavir and zidovudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. Atazanavir increases zileuton levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity. Cobicistat increases zuranolone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir also elevates zuranolone levels through the same mechanism. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
